events.content:
This is a Next.js 16 app with `cacheComponents: true` (PPR-style partial prerendering). Right now the whole `Project` component awaits both `getProjectTitle` and `getProjectDetails` together inside one `Suspense`, and both data functions use `'use cache'` — so the entire page (title *and* activity feed) resolves statically and gets fully prefetched as one unit.

To get "title prefetches instantly, rest doesn't," I need to split the title into its own cached, statically-prefetchable piece, and make the details genuinely dynamic (not cached) inside its own separate `Suspense` boundary, so Next's partial prefetch only fills the static shell (the title) and defers the details fetch to actual navigation time.

events.content:
Build confirms it: `/projects/[slug]` now shows `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — the title is prerendered as static shell (instant on prefetch), while activity/details streams dynamically at navigation time and is excluded from prefetch.

Summary of the fix in `app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` and `lib/data.ts`:
- Split the single `Project` component into `ProjectTitle` and `ProjectDetails`, each with their own `Suspense` boundary.
- Kept `getProjectTitle` under `'use cache'` so it resolves at prerender time and ships in the static shell Next prefetches on link hover/viewport.
- Removed `'use cache'` from `getProjectDetails`, making it a genuine dynamic hole — Next only fetches it on actual navigation, not during prefetch.
